scenario: AITA for not making my 7 year old brother go to sleep? | For context I (18M) have a brother who's 7, he's pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he gets less sleep than normal he will be all out of sorts the next day. In typical little sibling fashion my brother is obsessed with my friends, he thinks they are just the coolest and always wants to hang out with us. My friends who don't have little siblings think he's so cute and always hype him up and stuff. Last night my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until like 1am, and she said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on time (he can put himself to bed) and then my friend came over. We were goofing around and watching a movie and being kind of loud so my brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, I said no go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing/ exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us, by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning he didn't want to get up (even on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7 he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later he will not feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age was not a big deal. AITA for not forcing him to go to bed?

message.reasoning:
Hmm, this is a moral evaluation scenario where the user is asking whether it was acceptable for an 18-year-old brother to not enforce bedtime for his 7-year-old sibling. The user has provided detailed context about the situation.

Okay, let me break this down. The core issue is about responsibility and consequences. The older brother was left in charge, knew the younger sibling is sensitive to sleep deprivation, but chose not to enforce bedtime because it would have been difficult and embarrassing to do so. Instead, he let the younger brother stay up late, resulting in the child being cranky the next day.

From a moral standpoint, when someone is entrusted with responsibility for a child's wellbeing, they have a duty to prioritize that child's needs over convenience. The older brother had several options: he could have firmly enforced bedtime despite the resistance, or he could have found a compromise that didn't involve sacrificing the child's sleep. Instead, he chose the path of least resistance, which directly harmed the younger brother's wellbeing the next day.

The fact that the younger brother is "sensitive" to sleep makes this even more significant - the older brother was aware of the likely negative consequences but chose to ignore them for his own convenience. The mother's anger is understandable given this breach of trust.

While the older brother tries to justify it by saying "2 hours of missed sleep... was not a big deal" and that the child should learn consequences, these arguments don't hold up. A 7-year-old doesn't have the capacity to fully understand sleep consequences, and the responsibility ultimately falls on the caregiver (in this case, the temporary caregiver) to ensure proper care.

Therefore, the action was morally unacceptable. The older brother failed in his duty of care by prioritizing his own comfort over his brother's wellbeing.
